items.note: The page defines frames, the edge change $D_vD_u^{-1}$, $D_{\rm in}$, $D_{\rm out}$, $\mathsf S_\Omega$ and $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$ as in the paper (lines 785-805). It gets the implemented operator $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$ by induction along the wires and concludes that the interior frames can be chosen 'purely to make each edge change inexpensive', which matches lines 806-825.

All three cases of the induction are shown. At a source the invariant holds by definition of $g$. On an edge the array goes from $D_u\varphi$ to $D_vD_u^{-1}D_u\varphi=D_v\varphi$. At a gate, 'because all incidences use the same frame', $\sum_j c_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_j c_j\varphi_j)$. The page then reads off $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$ at the sinks, following the paper's lines 806-817.

The page writes 'Suppose the scalar network is a signed role permutation ... Then that route applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$', and it keeps both the auxiliary roles and the fixed routing. It never reads this off as the $(\rho(w),w)$ block of $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$. The only argument it gives in between is a telescoping of edge operators along one route, which does not produce $\varepsilon_w$ and is not the paper's 'in particular' specialization of the identity.

errors.quote: A route through a vertex $m$ from a source $s$ to a sink $t$ applies $D_mD_s^{-1}$ and then $D_tD_m^{-1}$, whose product is $D_tD_s^{-1}$ for every $D_m$.
errors.problem: This multiplies only the edge operators and ignores the gate at $m$. In the exchange networks the gates combine a wire's array with others, and a signed role permutation comes out only as a net effect of such combinations, so a role's 'route' is not a single path of bare edge changes. In the paper the interior frames cancel because the pointwise gate commutes with the common frame $D_m$ (the invariant), which gives the identity $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$. The telescoping product also leaves out the sign $\varepsilon_w$ that $\mathsf S_\Omega$ contributes.
